Cell culture studies and gain-of-function mouse models suggest that canonical Wnt proteins modulate adipose tissue expansion.… 18450716 noncanonical-wnt-signaling-promotes-obesity-induced-adipose-tissue-inflammation-and-metabolic-dysfunction-independent-of-adipose-tissue-expansion noncanonical wnt signaling promotes obesity induced adipose tissue Adipose tissue dysfunction plays a pivotal role in the Noncanonical Wnt Signaling Promotes Obesity-Induced Adipose Tissue Inflammation and Metabolic Dysfunction Independent of Adipose Tissue Expansion Adipose tissue dysfunction plays a pivotal role in the development of insulin resistance in obese individuals. Cell culture studies and gain-of-function mouse models suggest that canonical Wnt proteins modulate adipose tissue expansion. However, no genetic evidence supports a role for endogenous Wnt proteins in adipose tissue dysfunction, and the role of noncanonical Wnt signaling remains largely unexplored. Here we provide evidence from human, mouse, and cell culture studies showing that Wnt5a-mediated, noncanonical Wnt signaling contributes to obesity-associated metabolic dysfunction by increasing adipose tissue inflammation.
